Between October 1 and October 31, 2026, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added a total of 36 vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog based on confirmed evidence of active exploitation in the wild [[33]](https://varaxontech.com/guides/cisa-kev-report-october-2026). This volume exceeded the 2026 monthly average of 27 additions, with 29 of the entries carrying a strict 3-day remediation deadline for U.S. federal agencies under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 [[33]](https://varaxontech.com/guides/cisa-kev-report-october-2026). The additions spanned a wide range of critical infrastructure, enterprise software, and foundational components. Below is the chronological listing of every CVE added during this period, along with the associated vendor and product.

### October 1–4, 2026
On October 1, CISA added **CVE-2026-104286**, a critical unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability allowing arbitrary file writes in **Fortinet FortiMail** [[51]](https://varaxontech.com/guides/cisa-kev-report-october-2026). Two days later, on October 2, two session hijacking and privilege escalation flaws, **CVE-2026-102489** and **CVE-2026-102490**, were added targeting **Zammad GmbH Zammad** [[76]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/02/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). On October 4, **CVE-2026-88779** was cataloged, affecting **Citrix NetScaler** appliances configured as SAML providers and enabling denial-of-service conditions [[127]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/04/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog).

### October 8, 2026
A significant batch of five legacy vulnerabilities was added on October 8 after being actively abused by the China-linked threat actor Flax Typhoon [[106]](https://eastbaycyber.com/kev/added/2026-10-08/). These included **CVE-2015-3306** (ProFTPD ProFTPD), **CVE-2015-5477** (ISC BIND), **CVE-2016-3081** (Apache Struts), **CVE-2021-3199** (ONLYOFFICE Docs), and **CVE-2023-22894** (Strapi Strapi) [[106]](https://eastbaycyber.com/kev/added/2026-10-08/).

### October 13–16, 2026
On October 13, CISA added **CVE-2026-104935**, an authentication bypass in **Ivanti Connect Secure**, alongside **CVE-2026-96951**, a command injection flaw in the **Microsoft Windows** Shell [[134]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/13/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). The following day, October 14, saw four additions: **CVE-2026-0322** (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), **CVE-2026-76519** (Cisco Secure Email Gateway), and a two-stage intrusion chain comprising **CVE-2026-105133** and **CVE-2026-105134** targeting **Ahsay AhsayCBS** [[185]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/14/cisa-adds-four-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). On October 15, **CVE-2026-21589** was added, impacting multiple **Atlassian** Data Center products through arbitrary file access [[190]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/15/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog). October 16 brought **CVE-2025-61624** (Fortinet Multiple Products) and **CVE-2026-102764**, an authentication bypass in **BeyondTrust Remote Support** [[153]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/16/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

### October 20–23, 2026
A major alert on October 20 added six vulnerabilities [[150]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/20/cisa-adds-six-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). This batch included **CVE-2026-106931** (EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition), **CVE-2026-110936** (Siemens Software Center), and four chained flaws fueling the Plex2Shell cryptojacking campaign: **CVE-2026-96652**, **CVE-2026-96654**, **CVE-2026-96655**, and **CVE-2026-96656**, all affecting **Plex Media Server** [[225]](https://eastbaycyber.com/kev/added/2026-10-20/). On October 23, two more entries were added: **CVE-2026-110447** (Collabora Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server) and **CVE-2026-114625** (Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator) [[177]](https://eastbaycyber.com/kev/added/2026-10-23/).

### October 26–30, 2026
On October 26, CISA added two critical memory-safety flaws in the PHP interpreter itself, **CVE-2026-109618** and **CVE-2026-109619**, prompting the FBI to recommend offline isolation for unpatched systems [[59]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). The next day, October 27, saw the addition of **CVE-2026-111497** (Google Brotli) and **CVE-2026-48356** (Adobe Commerce and Magento) [[58]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/27/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). On October 28, **CVE-2026-41709** (Broadcom VMware ESX) and **CVE-2026-46300** (Linux Kernel Linux Kernel) were cataloged [[29]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/28/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). October 29 brought **CVE-2026-76418** (Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software) and **CVE-2026-97229** (GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition) [[31]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/29/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). Finally, on October 30, two additional chained flaws were added to the catalog: **CVE-2026-111357** and **CVE-2026-118527**, both affecting **Ivanti Connect Secure** [[65]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/30/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

### Summary of Trends
The October 2026 additions highlight a shift toward rapid exploitation of legacy software, complex multi-stage attack chains (notably in Ivanti, Ahsay, and Plex), and critical flaws in foundational technologies like the Linux kernel, PHP, and Brotli [[33]](https://varaxontech.com/guides/cisa-kev-report-october-2026). CISA's aggressive 3-day remediation windows under BOD 26-04 underscore the heightened risk these actively exploited flaws pose to federal and civilian enterprises [[67]](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).
